_comment: File upload contract -- repeated field name -> a LIST (no silent drop), a
safe-save helper that confines the write, and a running per-chunk size guard.
Feature 44, UP-DEC-02 / UP-DEC-03 (OWNER-DECISIONS Batch 4).
Three data-loss / footgun defects the audit found in the multipart path, now
fixed in all four frameworks with real (no-mock) tests -- real multipart bytes
through the real parser, real temp files on the real filesystem, and a real
over-limit body refused as it arrives.
UP-MULTIFILE-LOSS (upload-repeated-field-list): two files posted under the SAME
field name silently lost all but the last in Python, Ruby and the PHP socket
server (result[name] = {...} overwrote). Only Node kept a list. Now all four
produce a LIST for a repeated file field name (Node's model); a single
occurrence stays a plain descriptor (backward compatible). Python parses the
list in _parse_multipart + _is_file_value; PHP in parseMultipartBody; Ruby
hand-scans the raw body (Rack's POST collapses a repeated non-bracket name to
last-wins, so the file extraction can no longer delegate that to Rack); Node
was already correct.
UP-FILENAME-UNTRUSTED (upload-safe-save-confines): the client filename reached
the descriptor verbatim and no framework save sanitised it. A save built from a
'../../evil' name wrote outside the target dir. Each framework now ships ONE
safe-save helper (Python save_upload, PHP Request::saveUpload, Ruby
Tina4::Request.save_upload, Node saveUpload) that strips directory components
from the untrusted name (so '../../evil' becomes 'evil' written INSIDE the
target dir), refuses an unusable name ('', '.', '..', a NUL byte), and confirms
the resolved parent is the target dir (realpath containment) before writing.
UP-CHUNKED-BYPASS (upload-per-chunk-size-guard): PHP and Ruby enforced the
upload cap on the DECLARED Content-Length only, so a chunked or under-declared
over-size body was buffered whole before being refused (or never refused).
Python and Node already ran a running per-chunk counter. PHP now counts the
ACTUAL body bytes as they arrive in Server::enforceRequestLimits (driven by
TINA4_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE) and answers 413 the moment they exceed the cap; Ruby
reads rack.input through read_stream_capped, which raises PayloadTooLarge the
moment the running total exceeds the cap (rescued into 413 by the pipeline).
Mutation-proved (all four): revert the repeated-field merge to last-wins and
'two files ... arrive as a list' goes RED (only one file survives); drop the
basename strip in the safe-save helper and 'safe save writes a traversal
filename inside the target dir' goes RED (the escaped path appears outside the
target dir); remove the running per-chunk counter (PHP enforceRequestLimits /
Ruby read_stream_capped) and 'an over limit upload is refused with 413' goes
RED (the over-limit body is accepted). Restoring each returns to green.
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework carrying the SAME case
names in each language's own idiom, which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py
normalises and matches.
feature: 44 - File upload (repeated field name -> list, safe-save helper, running per-chunk size guard)

invariants.rule: When a multipart body sends the SAME field name more than once, every uploaded file under that name is collected into a LIST (an array) in the files map -- no file is silently dropped. A field name that occurs exactly once stays a single descriptor (backward compatible). Proven by parsing a real multipart body carrying two files under one field name and asserting both arrive, plus a single-file control that stays a scalar descriptor.
invariants.why: Two files posted under one field name silently lost all but the last in Python (_parse_multipart), Ruby (extract_files) and the PHP socket server (parseMultipartBody) -- real data loss with no signal (UP-MULTIFILE-LOSS); only Node kept a list. The fix collects repeated file field names into a list in all four (Node's model), so an upload form with a repeated <input multiple> or a repeated field never drops a file. Mutation-proved: reverting the merge to last-wins makes only one file survive, turning the 'two files ... arrive as a list' case RED.
cases: two files under one field name arrive as a list
a single file stays a single descriptor

invariants.rule: The safe-save helper writes an uploaded file's content only INSIDE the target directory. It derives a safe name from the untrusted client filename by stripping directory components (both / and \), so a '../../evil' name is written as 'evil' inside the target dir and never escapes it; it refuses an unusable name ('', '.', '..', or one containing a NUL byte) by raising. Proven by saving with a traversal filename and asserting the file lands inside the target dir while the would-be escaped path does NOT exist, plus a negative case that an unusable name raises.
invariants.why: The client filename reached the file descriptor verbatim in all four with no sanitisation, and no framework save existed, so an application that saved to target_dir + client_filename could be driven to write outside target_dir with a '../' name (UP-FILENAME-UNTRUSTED). One safe-save helper per language (Python save_upload, PHP Request::saveUpload, Ruby Tina4::Request.save_upload, Node saveUpload) sanitises + confines. Mutation-proved: dropping the basename strip lets the traversal name write to the parent, so the escaped path exists and the case goes RED.
cases: safe save writes a traversal filename inside the target dir
safe save refuses an unusable filename

invariants.rule: An upload whose ACTUAL body exceeds TINA4_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE is refused with 413 as the bytes arrive (a running per-chunk counter), not after the whole body has been buffered -- so a body with an under-declared or absent Content-Length is still bounded. A body under the limit is accepted. Proven against a real server / real dispatch: an over-limit body (whose declared length does not itself trip the declared-length guard) answers 413, and a small body still serves.
invariants.why: PHP and Ruby enforced the cap on the DECLARED Content-Length only, so a chunked or under-declared over-size body bypassed it and was buffered whole (UP-CHUNKED-BYPASS); Python and Node already ran a running counter. PHP now counts actual body bytes in Server::enforceRequestLimits and Ruby reads rack.input through read_stream_capped, both refusing the moment the running total exceeds TINA4_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE. Mutation-proved: removing the running counter makes the over-limit body accepted, turning the 'an over limit upload is refused with 413' case RED.
cases: an over limit upload is refused with 413
a body under the limit is accepted
